claims.source: P35 hGFAP-cre;E545K and Nestin-cre;E545K brains were noticeably larger than controls, while Nestin-creER;E545K mutants had normal-sized brains compared to controls.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by visual and volumetric data in Figure 1e-h.

claims.claim: Nestin-creER;E545K mutants had normal-sized brains compared to controls.
claims.source: P35 hGFAP-cre;E545K and Nestin-cre;E545K brains were noticeably larger than controls, while Nestin-creER;E545K mutants had normal-sized brains compared to controls.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric data in Figure 1g,h.

claims.claim: hGFAP-cre;E545K mice had a milder phenotype than hGFAP-cre;H1047R mice, surviving as adults without hydrocephalus, though their brain size was significantly larger compared to control littermates.
claims.source: E545K mice with the same cre-driver (hGFAP-cre;E545K) had a milder phenotype, surviving as adults without hydrocephalus, though their brain size was significantly larger compared to control littermates (Figure 1e,h,j).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing E545K and H1047R phenotypes.

claims.claim: With identical time of activation by the same cre driver, the brain phenotypes are dependent on specific Pik3ca allele.
claims.source: This provides evidence that with identical time of activation by the same cre driver, the brain phenotypes are dependent on specific Pik3ca allele.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from comparing hGFAP-cre;H1047R and hGFAP-cre;E545K phenotypes.

claims.claim: Earlier activation of E545K mutation with Nestin-cre led to a 54.4% volumetric increase, with mild ventriculomegaly and no hydrocephalus.
claims.source: Earlier activation of E545K mutation with Nestin-cre led to an even more striking 54.4% volumetric increase, with mild ventriculomegaly and no hydrocephalus (Figure 1f,h,k).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric MRI data in Figure 1h.

claims.claim: Neonatal activation of E545K using Nestin-creER had no apparent impact on brain size.
claims.source: Interestingly, neonatal activation of E545K using Nestin-creER had no apparent impact on brain size (Figure 1g,h,l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric data in Figure 1h.

claims.claim: Enlarged head size in both Nestin-cre;E545K and hGFAP-cre;E545K mutants was evident at birth and brain size of all the three adult E545K mutants was relatively stable.
claims.source: Enlarged head size in both Nestin-cre;E545K and hGFAP-cre;E545K mutants was evident at birth and brain size of all the three adult E545K mutants was relatively stable (data not shown).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations not shown in figures.

claims.claim: Gross morphology was normal for all E545K mutants.
claims.source: Unlike H1047R mutants, gross morphology was normal for all E545K mutants.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by visual inspection of brain sections in Figure 1.

claims.claim: To cause brain overgrowth, overactivation of Pik3ca function is required during embryogenesis.
claims.source: Further, we conclude that to cause brain overgrowth, overactivation of Pik3ca function is required during embryogenesis.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the timing experiments showing no overgrowth with postnatal activation.

claims.claim: The inner cortical length of hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants was longer than controls at both E14.5 and E16.5.
claims.source: The inner cortical length of hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants was longer than controls at both E14.5 (p<0.01) and E16.5 (p<0.001; Figure 2b–g).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants showed enlarged nuclear and cell size at both E14.5 and E16.5.
claims.source: This was accompanied by enlarged nuclear and cell size at both ages and decreased cell density at E16.5, but not increased proliferation or cell cycle exit (Figure 3c–l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claims.claim: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants showed decreased cell density at E16.5.
claims.source: This was accompanied by enlarged nuclear and cell size at both ages and decreased cell density at E16.5, but not increased proliferation or cell cycle exit (Figure 3c–l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claims.claim: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants did not show increased proliferation or cell cycle exit.
claims.source: This was accompanied by enlarged nuclear and cell size at both ages and decreased cell density at E16.5, but not increased proliferation or cell cycle exit (Figure 3c–l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claims.claim: Total cell number per cortical column length was not significantly different between control and H1047R mutant both at E14.5 and E16.5.
claims.source: Total cell number per cortical column length was not significantly different between control and H1047R mutant both at E14.5 and E16.5.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: TUNEL+ cell number was significantly lower in E16.5 H1047R mutant cortex than in control.
claims.source: Also, TUNEL+ cell number was significantly lower in E16.5 mutant cortex than in control (p<0.01), indicating reduced apoptosis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a,c); however the overall TUNEL+ cell numbers for both control and mutant were small.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative TUNEL data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Cortical expansion in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutant was not primarily driven by increased proliferation or reduced apoptosis; rather reduced cell density and increased cell size during embryogenesis were major contributing factors.
claims.source: Together these results indicate that cortical expansion in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutant was not primarily driven by increased proliferation or reduced apoptosis; rather reduced cell density and increased cell size during embryogenesis were major contributing factors.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined developmental data.

claims.claim: In Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, the inner cortical length was comparable to controls at E14.5 but elongated at E16.5.
claims.source: By contrast, in Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, the inner cortical length was comparable to controls at E14.5 but elongated at E16.5 (p<0.01); cortical thickness was slightly reduced in E16.5 (p<0.05) as compared to controls (Figure 2h–m).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Cortical thickness was slightly reduced in E16.5 Nestin-cre;E545K mutants as compared to controls.
claims.source: By contrast, in Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, the inner cortical length was comparable to controls at E14.5 but elongated at E16.5 (p<0.01); cortical thickness was slightly reduced in E16.5 (p<0.05) as compared to controls (Figure 2h–m).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements in Figure 2.

claims.claim: The labeling index was similar to the control at E14.5 but increased in E16.5 Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, indicating more proliferation.
claims.source: The labeling index was similar to the control at E14.5 but increased in E16.5 mutants (p<0.05), indicating more proliferation (Figure 3m,o,r).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU labeling data in Figure 3.

claims.claim: Cell density in E545K mutant neocortex was similar to the control at E14.5 but was reduced at E16.5.
claims.source: Cell density in E545K mutant neocortex was similar to the control at E14.5 but was reduced at E16.5 (p<0.05).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claims.claim: Total cells per cortical column length did not change in the E545K mutant.
claims.source: Total cells per cortical column length did not change in the E545K mutant; but the TUNEL+ cell number was lower in E16.5 mutant cortex than in control (p<0.001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: TUNEL+ cell number was lower in E16.5 E545K mutant cortex than in control.
claims.source: Total cells per cortical column length did not change in the E545K mutant; but the TUNEL+ cell number was lower in E16.5 mutant cortex than in control (p<0.001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative TUNEL data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The nuclear size of E545K mutant cells was similar to controls at both E14.5 and E16.5 but cell somas were significantly larger at E16.5.
claims.source: Intriguingly, the nuclear size of these mutant cells was similar to controls at both E14.5 and E16.5 but cell somas were significantly larger (p<0.05) at E16.5 (Figure 3n,p,q,s,t).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements in Figure 3.

claims.claim: The quit fraction indicative of rate of cells exiting cell cycle was significantly higher in the E545K mutant between E15.5 and E16.5.
claims.source: The quit fraction indicative of rate of cells exiting cell cycle was significantly higher (p<0.05) in the E545K mutant between E15.5 and E16.5 (Figure 3u,v).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cell cycle exit data in Figure 3.

claims.claim: At P35, the neocortical cells of Nestin-cre;E545K mutant were larger compared to controls.
claims.source: At P35, the neocortical cells of Nestin-cre;E545K mutant were still larger (p<0.05) compared to controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a,b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: In the adult P35 Nestin-creER;E545K mutant mice, where activation was initiated in neonates and brain size was not different from controls, E545K-activated (YFP+) cells have the same size as controls.
claims.source: Notably, in the adult P35 Nestin-creER;E545K mutant mice, where activation was initiated in neonates, and brain size was not different from controls, E545K-activated (YFP+) cells have the same size as controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2c,d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Increased cell size due to E545K overactivation has a critical embryonic period.
claims.source: We conclude that increased cell size due to E545K overactivation also has a critical embryonic period.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the timing experiments showing no cell size increase with postnatal activation.

claims.claim: Changes in multiple developmental parameters including proliferation, cell cycle exit, cell size and density contribute to MEG of Nestin-cre;E545K Pik3ca embryonic overactivation.
claims.source: Further, changes in multiple developmental parameters including proliferation, cell cycle exit, cell size and density contribute to MEG of Nestin-cre;E545K Pik3ca embryonic overactivation.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined developmental data for E545K mutants.

claims.claim: Disordered lamination is a key feature of human SEGCD.
claims.source: Since disordered lamination is a key feature of human SEGCD (Arai et al., 2012; Rossini et al., 2014), we assessed neocortical organization and development in both hGFAP-cre;H1047R and Nestin-cre;E545K mutants.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on human SEGCD pathology.

claims.claim: In H1047R mutants, the radial glial scaffold was slightly fasciculated and irregular at E14.5 and E16.5.
claims.source: In H1047R mutants, the radial glial scaffold was slightly fasciculated and irregular at E14.5 and E16.5.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Irregularities in radial glial scaffold were very prominent at P0 in H1047R mutants when a disrupted pial surface was associated with irregular clusters of enlarged radial glial end-feet.
claims.source: Irregularities were very prominent at P0 when a disrupted pial surface was associated with irregular clusters of enlarged radial glial end-feet (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The radial glial phenotype was much more subtle in the E545K mutant at E14.5 and E16.5.
claims.source: The radial glial phenotype was much more subtle in the E545K mutant at E14.5 and E16.5; however at P0, we observed thinning of radial glial fibers and irregular clusters of end-feet at the intact pial surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: At P0, E545K mutants showed thinning of radial glial fibers and irregular clusters of end-feet at the intact pial surface.
claims.source: The radial glial phenotype was much more subtle in the E545K mutant at E14.5 and E16.5; however at P0, we observed thinning of radial glial fibers and irregular clusters of end-feet at the intact pial surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Cajal-Retzius cells expressing Reelin were normally present in an ordered array in the marginal zone (layer I) of controls and Nestin-cre;E545K mice.
claims.source: Cajal-Retzius cells expressing Reelin, a major regulator of radial migration, were normally present in an ordered array in the marginal zone (layer I) of controls and Nestin-cre;E545K mice (Figure 4b; Figure 5b,c).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figures 4 and 5.

claims.claim: Cajal-Retzius cells were dysplastic in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mice at E16.5.
claims.source: However, these cells were dysplastic in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mice at E16.5 (Figure 4c,c').
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Ectopic Reelin-positive cells were not observed within the cortical column in either mutant.
claims.source: We did not observe ectopic Reelin-positive cells within the cortical column in either mutant.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of immunohistochemical data.

claims.claim: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants displayed a marked disorganization of all layers with Ctip2/Tbr1-positive as well as Cux1-positive cells dispersed throughout the cortical plate.
claims.source: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants displayed a marked disorganization of all layers. Ctip2/Tbr1-positive as well as Cux1-positive cells in the E16.5 H1047R mutant were dispersed throughout the cortical plate, with both early- and late-born neurons severely mislocalized (Figure 4d–g).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Laminar disorganization was less severe in E16.5 Nestin-cre;E545K brains, but deep Ctip2/Tbr1-positive neurons and upper Cux1-positive neurons were dispersed throughout the cortical plate.
claims.source: Laminar disorganization was less severe in E16.5 Nestin-cre;E545K brains, but deep Ctip2/Tbr1-positive neurons and upper Cux1-positive neurons were dispersed throughout the cortical plate (Figure 5f,g).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Laminar patterns in postnatal animals remained disrupted in both mutants, with hGFAP-cre;H1047R cortex more affected than Nestin-cre;E545K mutant cortex.
claims.source: Laminar patterns in postnatal animals remained disrupted in both mutants, with hGFAP-cre;H1047R cortex more affected Nestin-cre;E545K mutant cortex (Figure 5h–m).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figures 4 and 5.

claims.claim: A simple developmental delay was not the cause of dysplasia.
claims.source: Thus a simple developmental delay was not the cause of dysplasia (Figure 4h–m; Figure 5h–m).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the persistence of dysplasia in postnatal animals.

claims.claim: In P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, NeuN-positive mature cortical neurons were found within the normally cell-sparse marginal zone as well as in the cortical white matter and residual ventricular zone.
claims.source: In P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, NeuN-positive mature cortical neurons were found within the normally cell-sparse marginal zone as well as in the cortical white matter and residual ventricular zone, a feature reported in SEGCD patients (Arai et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4 and comparison to human pathology.

claims.claim: The cortical subplate was not readily discernible in P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, blurring the boundary between grey and white matter.
claims.source: Further, the cortical subplate was not readily discernible in these mutants (Figure 4h–k; Figure 4—figure supplement 2e,f), blurring the boundary between grey and white matter – a feature often observed in SEGCD patients (Rossini et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4 and comparison to human pathology.

claims.claim: The total numbers of BrdU+ P0 cells, born at E12.5 and E16.5, were not significantly different between controls and either hGFAP-cre;H1047R or Nestin-cre;E545K mutants.
claims.source: The total numbers of BrdU+ P0 cells, born at E12.5 and E16.5, were not significantly different between controls and either hGFAP-cre;H1047R or Nestin-cre;E545K mutants (Figure 6b,j).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The distribution of BrdU+ cells showed significant differences between controls and H1047R mutants labelled during both early and late embryonic stages.
claims.source: The distribution of BrdU+ cells showed significant differences between controls and H1047R mutants labelled during both early and late embryonic stages. At P0, more BrdU+ cells were localized in the lower cortical plate (CP) and white matter (Figure 6c).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: For E545K mutants the BrdU+ cell numbers were not different at either age, but the distribution was subtly yet significantly different only for the early born neurons.
claims.source: For E545K mutants the BrdU+ cell numbers were not different at either age. The distribution was subtly, yet significantly different only for the early born neurons (Figure 6k).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: For both the H1047R and E545K Pik3ca activating alleles, total layer V (Ctip2+) cell numbers at P0 were not significantly different between controls and mutants.
claims.source: For both the H1047R and E545K Pik3ca activating alleles, total layer V (Ctip2+) cell numbers at P0 were not significantly different between controls and mutants (Figure 6d,l).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The numbers of Ctip2/BrdU double-labeled cells were the same in controls and mutants, indicating that cell fate specification for these deep layer neurons was unaffected by either the H1047R or E545K Pik3ca allele.
claims.source: Also, the numbers of Ctip2/BrdU double-labeled cells were the same in controls and mutants, indicating that cell fate specification for these deep layer neurons was unaffected by either the H1047R or E545K Pik3ca allele (Figure 6e,m).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the birthdating data showing normal numbers of fate-specified neurons.

claims.claim: The specific distribution of layer V neurons was abnormal in H1047R mutants, with ectopic Ctip2/BrdU double-labeled cells in the upper and lower CP and white matter, instead of mid CP.
claims.source: However, similar to the overall BrdU+ cell distribution, the specific distribution of layer V neurons was abnormal in H1047R mutants, with ectopic Ctip2/BrdU double-labeled cells in the upper and lower CP and white matter, instead of mid CP (Figure 6f).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: In E545K mutants, fewer Ctip2+ cells were positioned in the mid CP, although the phenotype was much less severe than H1047R.
claims.source: In E545K mutants, fewer Ctip2+ cells were positioned in the mid CP (Figure 6n), although the phenotype was much less severe.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Upper layer (Cux1+) neuronal numbers and distributions were significantly different in both H1047R and E545K mutants, compared to their respective controls.
claims.source: Upper layer (Cux1+) neuronal numbers and distributions were significantly different in both H1047R and E545K mutants, compared to their respective controls (Figure 6g,o).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: In E545K mutants, the increase in total Cux1+ cell numbers corresponded to increased Cux1/BrdU double-labeled cells, born at E16.5.
claims.source: In E545K mutants, the increase in total Cux1+ cell numbers in the E545K mutant corresponded to increased Cux1/BrdU double-labeled cells, born at E16.5 (Figure 6p).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: No correlation was observed between Cux1+ cell numbers and Cux1/BrdU double-labeled cells in E12.5 or E16.5-born cells in the H1047R mutant.
claims.source: However, no such correlation was observed in E12.5 or E16.5-born Cux1+ cells in the H1047R mutant (Figure 6h).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Extra Cux1+ cells in H1047R mutants were likely born between E16.5 and P0.
claims.source: These extra cells were therefore likely born between E16.5 and P0.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the birthdating data.

claims.claim: Cell fates are largely correctly specified in both Pik3ca mutants and cortical dysplasia is more likely caused by aberrant neuronal migration.
claims.source: Together, these data indicate that cell fates are largely correctly specified in both Pik3ca mutants and that cortical dysplasia is more likely caused by aberrant neuronal migration.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined birthdating and lamination data.

claims.claim: In P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, the underlying cortical white matter was much thicker than controls, although the cortical plate itself was not dramatically thicker.
claims.source: In P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, although the cortical plate itself was not dramatically thicker than controls, the underlying cortical white matter was much thicker (Figure 4j,k; Figure 4—figure suplement 2e,f).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4.

claims.claim: White matter thickening was less pronounced but readily discernible in P3 Nestin-cre;E545K mutants.
claims.source: This was less pronounced but readily discernible in P3 Nestin-cre;E545K mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2c,d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: In P3 H1047R mutants, there was complete absence of corpus callosum, although hippocampal and anterior commissures were present.
claims.source: In P3 H1047R mutants, there was complete absence of corpus callosum, although hippocampal and anterior commissures were present (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a-d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: All major tracts were present in P3 E545K mutants.
claims.source: In contrast, all major tracts were present in P3 E545K mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The white matter phenotypes are consistent with the wide spectrum of white matter dysplasia reported in MEG and SEGCD patients.
claims.source: These data are consistent with the wide spectrum of white matter dysplasia reported in MEG and SEGCD patients (Conway et al., 2007; Adamsbaum et al., 1998; De Rosa et al., 1992; Jansen et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on comparison to human pathology cited in the literature.

claims.claim: Increased number of Olig2-positive cells was observed in the white matter area of both H1047R and E545K mutants.
claims.source: Moreover, increased number of Olig2-positive cells was observed in the white matter area of both H1047R and E545K mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in the figure supplements.

claims.claim: Astrocytosis is not a feature of PIK3CA-pathology in the mouse models.
claims.source: Although astrocytosis is observed when mTOR signaling is activated by TSC mutations in humans and mice (Sosunov et al., 2008; Zeng et al., 2008), it is not a feature of PIK3CA-pathology in our mouse models (Figure 5—figure supplement 3a-d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Epilepsy is one of the most important clinical features of SEGCD.
claims.source: Epilepsy is one of the most important clinical features of SEGCD (Bast et al., 2006; Fauser et al., 2015; Fauser, 2006; Arai et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on SEGCD.

claims.claim: Baseline sleep EEG recordings in both Nestin-cre;E545K and Nestin-creER;E545K animal models revealed epileptiform activity including sets of spikes/polyspikes, and regional and generalized spike and wave discharges during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
claims.source: Baseline sleep EEG recordings in both animal models revealed epileptiform activity including sets of spikes/polyspikes, and regional and generalized spike and wave discharges during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep (Figure 7b,c).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by EEG data in Figure 7.

claims.claim: The frequency of epileptiform interictal activity was increased in post sleep deprivation EEG recordings in Nestin-creER;E545K mice.
claims.source: The frequency of epileptiform interictal activity was increased in post sleep deprivation EEG recordings, and clinically relevant spontaneous seizures including myoclonic (MC) seizures, frequent isolated spikes, and train of spikes, were observed in the Nestin-creER;E545K mice (Figure 7d,e).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by EEG data in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Clinically relevant spontaneous seizures including myoclonic (MC) seizures, frequent isolated spikes, and train of spikes, were observed in the Nestin-creER;E545K mice after sleep deprivation.
claims.source: The frequency of epileptiform interictal activity was increased in post sleep deprivation EEG recordings, and clinically relevant spontaneous seizures including myoclonic (MC) seizures, frequent isolated spikes, and train of spikes, were observed in the Nestin-creER;E545K mice (Figure 7d,e).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by EEG data in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Both the megalencephalic and normocephalic E545K mouse models exhibited lower seizure thresholds compared to controls at both P35 and P180 when challenged with PTZ.
claims.source: When challenged with the chemoconvulsant pentylenetetrazol (PTZ), a GABA-A receptor antagonist (Macdonald and Barker, 1978), both the megalencephalic and normocephalic E545K mouse models exhibited lower seizure thresholds compared to controls at both P35 and P180 (Figure 7f–i; Figure 7—figure supplement 1d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by PTZ seizure induction data in Figure 7.

claims.claim: In the 30 min post PTZ injection, both E545K models showed shorter latencies to first generalized tonic clonic (GTC) seizures, more myoclonic seizures, and a prolonged seizure load.
claims.source: In the 30 min post PTZ injection, both models showed shorter latencies to first generalized tonic clonic (GTC) seizures, more myoclonic seizures, and a prolonged seizure load.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by PTZ seizure data in Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Pik3ca overactivation is sufficient to cause epilepsy.
claims.source: We conclude that Pik3ca overactivation is sufficient to cause epilepsy.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the epilepsy phenotypes observed in the mouse models.

claims.claim: Pik3ca-related epilepsy is dissociable from brain overgrowth and cortical dysplasia.
claims.source: Further our data indicate that Pik3ca-related epilepsy is dissociable from brain overgrowth and cortical dysplasia.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observation that normocephalic Nestin-creER;E545K mice also have epilepsy.

claims.claim: BKM120 is an orally available pan-Class I PI3K inhibitor currently in clinical trials for solid tumors.
claims.source: BKM120, a 2,6-dimorpholino pyrimidine derivative, is an orally available pan-Class I PI3K inhibitor currently in clinical trials for solid tumors (Maira et al., 2012; Bendell et al., 2012; Brachmann et al., 2012) and may represent a novel therapeutic agent for PIK3CA-related epilepsy.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on BKM120.

claims.claim: Preclinical studies show that BKM120 maximally inhibits downstream phosphorylation of Akt, 1hr post-administration.
claims.source: Preclinical studies show that BKM120 maximally inhibits downstream phosphorylation of Akt, 1hr post-administration (Maira et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on BKM120 pharmacodynamics.

claims.claim: BKM120 increased the seizure threshold of control animals.
claims.source: BKM120 increased the seizure threshold of control animals.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by PTZ seizure data in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Despite the presence of megalencephaly and considerable cortical dysplasia in P35 Nestin-cre;E545K megencephalic animals, BKM120 dramatically decreased the seizure number and duration to untreated control levels and marginally increased seizure latency in the mutant mice.
claims.source: More importantly, despite the presence of megalencephaly and considerable cortical dysplasia in P35 Nestin-cre;E545K megencephalic animals, BKM120 dramatically decreased the seizure number and duration to untreated control levels and marginally increased seizure latency in the mutant mice (Figure 7h,i; Figure 7—figure supplement 1d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by BKM120 treatment data in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Dynamic Pik3ca-dependent processes, independent of cortical and cellular dysplasia, cause Pik3ca-related epilepsy and they are highly amenable to therapeutic intervention.
claims.source: These data powerfully demonstrate that dynamic Pik3ca-dependent processes, independent of cortical and cellular dysplasia, cause Pik3ca-related epilepsy and they are highly amenable to therapeutic intervention.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the BKM120 treatment results.

claims.claim: Untreated Nestin-cre;E545K mutants exhibited significant elevations of phospho (p)S473-Akt and pT346-NDRG1, consistent with PI3K pathway activation.
claims.source: As expected, untreated Nestin-cre;E545K mutants exhibited significant elevations of phospho (p)S473-Akt and pT346-NDRG1, consistent with PI3K pathway activation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RPPA data in Figure 8.

results.result: PIK3CA mutations and other PI3K-AKT pathway components are associated with cancer and a spectrum of brain and body overgrowth disorders, collectively termed PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS). In the brain, these include severe segmental cortical dysplasia (SEGCD) such as megalencephaly, hemimegalencephaly, and focal cortical dysplasia, which is a leading cause of intractable pediatric epilepsy.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C16 establish the clinical and scientific background for PIK3CA-related disorders through citations to established literature. These are well-documented associations in the field and provide appropriate context for the experimental work.

results.result: Mouse models expressing H1047R and E545K Pik3ca mutations in neural progenitors recapitulate key human pathological features including brain enlargement, cortical malformation, hydrocephalus, and epilepsy. The H1047R mutation produces more severe phenotypes than E545K, with phenotypic severity dependent on both the specific mutant allele and the developmental timing of activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C36 and C108 are well-supported by extensive phenotypic characterization across multiple mouse models with different cre drivers and activation times. The data in Figures 1 and supplementary figures demonstrate clear allele-specific and timing-dependent differences in brain size, morphology, and survival.

results.result: Embryonic mechanisms underlying Pik3ca-related brain overgrowth differ between H1047R and E545K alleles. H1047R causes cortical expansion primarily through increased cell size and decreased cell density without increased proliferation, while E545K involves multiple parameters including increased proliferation, cell cycle exit, cell size, and reduced density at E16.5. Both mutations require embryonic activation to affect brain and cell size.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C55 are supported by comprehensive developmental analyses in Figures 2-3 with quantitative measurements of cortical dimensions, proliferation indices, cell cycle exit, cell size, and density at multiple embryonic timepoints. The data clearly demonstrate allele-specific mechanisms and critical developmental windows.

results.result: Embryonic Pik3ca activation causes cortical dysplasia with disrupted lamination in both H1047R and E545K mutants, with H1047R showing more severe disorganization. Features include abnormal radial glial scaffolds, dysplastic Cajal-Retzius cells (in H1047R), dispersed cortical neurons throughout layers, ectopic neurons in white matter, and blurred grey-white matter boundaries.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C69 are well-supported by detailed immunohistochemical analyses in Figures 4-5 showing layer-specific markers (Reelin, Ctip2, Tbr1, Cux1, NeuN) at embryonic and postnatal stages. The data demonstrate persistent laminar disorganization that is not due to developmental delay.

results.result: Birthdating studies demonstrate that cortical dysplasia in Pik3ca mutants results primarily from aberrant neuronal migration rather than altered cell fate specification. Total numbers of layer-specific neurons (Ctip2+ and Cux1+) are largely normal, but their spatial distributions are abnormal, with late-born neurons more severely affected than early-born neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C81 and C118-C121 are supported by comprehensive BrdU birthdating experiments in Figure 6 showing normal total cell numbers but abnormal distributions. The conclusion that migration rather than fate specification is disrupted is a reasonable inference from the data, though direct migration assays would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: Pik3ca mutations cause white matter dysplasia with increased white matter thickness and Olig2+ cells in both H1047R and E545K mutants. H1047R mutants show complete absence of corpus callosum while other commissures are present, whereas E545K mutants have all major tracts present. These features recapitulate the spectrum of white matter abnormalities in human MEG and SEGCD patients.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C88 and C124-C125 are supported by histological data in Figures 4-5 and supplements showing white matter phenotypes. The comparison to human pathology is appropriate based on cited literature, though astrocytosis is notably absent unlike in TSC-related mTOR activation.

results.result: Both megalencephalic (Nestin-cre;E545K) and normocephalic (Nestin-creER;E545K) E545K mouse models exhibit spontaneous epileptiform activity and lowered seizure thresholds to PTZ challenge, demonstrating that Pik3ca-related epilepsy is dissociable from brain overgrowth and cortical dysplasia.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C96, C19, and C126-C130 are strongly supported by EEG recordings and PTZ seizure induction experiments in Figure 7. The key finding that normocephalic mice with postnatal activation also have epilepsy provides compelling evidence that epilepsy is independent of structural malformations. Sample sizes appear adequate (n≥5 per group).

results.result: Acute 1-hour administration of the pan-PI3K inhibitor BKM120 dramatically suppresses PTZ-induced seizures in adult megalencephalic mice despite ongoing dysplasia, demonstrating that Pik3ca-related epilepsy represents an active, dynamically modulated process independent of structural pathology.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C20, C97-C101, C131, C140-C143, and C151 are well-supported by the BKM120 treatment experiments in Figure 7 showing normalized seizure thresholds, reduced seizure number and duration in mutants treated with BKM120. This is a paradigm-shifting finding, though the mechanism requires further elucidation and the clinical translatability needs validation.

results.result: RPPA analysis reveals that untreated E545K mutants have elevated PI3K signaling with preferential upregulation of mTOR-dependent pS473-Akt (especially in hippocampus). PTZ treatment increases phosphorylation of multiple pathway components in both mutants and controls, while acute BKM120 treatment inhibits these increases and returns mutant hippocampal pS473-Akt to baseline control levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C106 and C133-C137 are supported by comprehensive RPPA data in Figure 8 showing phosphorylation states of multiple PI3K pathway components across treatments. The modest baseline changes are consistent with prior cancer studies. However, the mechanistic link between these signaling changes and epilepsy requires further investigation.

results.result: The phenotypic differences between H1047R and E545K alleles reflect distinct mechanisms of PI3K activation rather than expression level differences. H1047R increases the level and duration of response to extracellular ligands, while E545K causes constitutive low-level signaling with blunted ligand response.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C110 are supported by the authors' reasoning about PI3K enzyme structure and citations to biochemical studies of these mutations. The argument that p85 levels limit p110 stability is sound, though direct measurement of pathway activation levels in the mouse models would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: PIK3CA-related brain overgrowth and increased cell size require embryonic activation of Pik3ca mutations in neural progenitors. Postnatal activation has no impact on brain or cell size, demonstrating a critical embryonic developmental window.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C113, C36, and C54 are well-supported by the timing experiments comparing embryonic versus postnatal activation across multiple cre drivers. The data clearly show that postnatal activation (Nestin-creER) does not cause megalencephaly or increased cell size.

results.result: Neuronal enlargement in Pik3ca mutants is less pronounced than in Pten null mice or Akt-overexpressing neurons, with brain size evident at birth without progressive postnatal increases. This pattern differs from Pten models and matches human SEGCD pathology where PIK3CA mutations cause milder cellular enlargement than PTEN or AKT3 mutations.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C117 appropriately compare the mouse phenotypes to other genetic models and human pathology based on cited literature. The comparison is valid and helps contextualize the severity of phenotypes, though direct side-by-side comparisons would be more definitive.

results.result: While the mouse models recapitulate many features of human SEGCD including ectopic neurons in subcortical white matter, the human phenotype of late-migrating neurons failing to reach upper layers is more severe than observed in the mouse models.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C123 appropriately acknowledge limitations of the mouse models compared to human pathology. The presence of ectopic neurons in white matter is confirmed by NeuN staining, while the comparison to human severity is based on cited literature.

results.result: The discovery that Pik3ca-related epilepsy is independent of dysplasia and amenable to acute pharmacological modulation represents a paradigm-shifting finding with potential therapeutic implications for intractable pediatric epilepsy, including patients with mTOR and AKT3 mutations. Current treatments (surgery, rapamycin) have limitations that PI3K inhibitors might address.
results.evaluation: Claims C138-C150 discuss the broader significance and therapeutic potential. While the mouse data (C7, C20, C100) strongly support acute efficacy of BKM120, the translational claims (C8, C145, C148, C151) are speculative. Clinical trials would be needed to validate therapeutic potential in humans, and long-term safety/efficacy of PI3K inhibitors for epilepsy is unknown. The paradigm shift regarding epilepsy mechanisms is supported by the data.

results.result: The underlying mechanisms of Pik3ca-related brain overgrowth include allele-specific combinations of increased proliferation, cell size, altered cell density, and white matter changes. Cortical dysplasia results primarily from aberrant neuronal migration rather than altered cell fate specification. Epilepsy represents an active Pik3ca-driven process that can be restricted by dynamic modulation of PI3K pathway activity.
results.evaluation: These summary/conclusion claims (C6, C21, C43, C55, C81, C120) are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented throughout the manuscript. They represent reasonable syntheses of the mechanistic findings, though some aspects (particularly the epilepsy mechanism) would benefit from additional investigation.

results.result: PI3K inhibitors offer a promising new avenue for effective anti-epileptic therapy for intractable pediatric epilepsy patients, representing a major paradigm shift in treatment approach. The mouse models serve as surrogates for patients with segmental brain overgrowth including those with mTOR and AKT3 mutations.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C144-C145, C148, and C151 make strong translational claims based on acute mouse studies. While the preclinical data are compelling, these claims are speculative without human clinical trials. The statement that models represent surrogates for all PI3K-AKT pathway disorders (C145) is an inference that requires validation. Long-term efficacy, safety, optimal dosing, and patient selection criteria are unknown.
